verdicts.note: Pamphlet 'fair taxation' (S1) plus S4: 'I back the recently passed millionaires tax ... I support flipping that system'. Repeated, explicit statements support +2/high.

S4 lists a broad set of expansions: WFTC, Working Connections Child Care eligibility, childcare-worker pay, early learning and after-school funding, affordable-housing construction, shelter capacity, homeownership aid and more L&I resources. It ties tax reform to 'unlocking the revenue we need to make all of these investments possible'. That is pole_b's 'invest and expand as the primary lever'. +2 holds at medium (platform only, no record).
Public funding and tenant protections (pole_b) alongside GMA reform for middle density (supply) give +1.
Root causes, gun buybacks, community-led programs and wraparound services, with no enforcement planks. +1 is, if anything, conservative.
General 'immediate action that reduces carbon emissions' with no CCA position, so +1/medium.
No elected office; running for 'new leadership' against a four-term incumbent.
Explicit sanctuary pledge regardless of immigration status (S4).

Reproductive policy only, but explicit: 'push back against any effort to limit reproductive autonomy', preserve and expand access, care as 'not a privilege'. +2/medium is consistent with Anderson's score. Bushnell's similar pro-choice pledge in Position 2 is scored +1; the coordinator may want to align the two.

Cached House roll calls confirm Morgan nay on ESSB 6346 final passage (Mena yea), and yea on ESSB 5096 (all three final votes, 2021), ESSB 5813, ESSB 5814 and ESHB 2081 (2025). Four recorded yea votes on progressive revenue (capital gains, estate, services, B&O surcharge) against one nay on the income tax make +1/medium a fair net. The score is not inferred from party: it rests on her own record, which diverges from her seatmate's. Roll calls not in the dossier (ESSB 5801 and several ESSB 6346 floor amendments where she split from Mena) were not used, because scoring is dossier-only; they are reported to the coordinator.
Pamphlet cites appropriations for the district (S1), and the caucus bio (S3) credits her with the $200M Community Reinvestment Account. +1/medium.
Both votes confirmed (EHB 1217 final passage as recommended by the conference committee, yea; E2SHB 1110, yea) and both are cited in her pamphlet statement.
I-2113 nay is confirmed, and the CRA funds violence prevention and reentry. Her pamphlet also claims 'public safety investments', which is direction-neutral, so +1/medium rather than more.
